title: Directives
summary: Repeat, show, hide, style and react to clicks with ng-repeat, ng-if, ng-show, ng-class and ng-click.

quiz.q: What is the main difference between `ng-if` and `ng-show`?
options: ng-if removes the element from the page, ng-show only hides it with CSS
ng-if is for numbers, ng-show is for text
ng-show removes the element, ng-if hides it
quiz.explain: `ng-if` adds or removes the element in the DOM. `ng-show` keeps it there and toggles the `ng-hide` CSS class. Use `ng-show` for things that toggle often.

quiz.q: Complete the list so it creates one `li` for each student in `students`.
With `$scope.marks = [70, 85, 90]`, how many list items does this produce? Type the number.
quiz.explain: `ng-repeat` creates one copy of the element per array item, so three.

quiz.q: Put the lines in order to make a button that increases a counter.
quiz.explain: Set the starting value, then define a function on the scope. A template can call it with `ng-click="increase()"`.

quiz.q: The button should call `toggle()` when clicked, but nothing happens. Click the faulty line.
quiz.explain: The plain `onclick` looks for a global function. A scope function needs `ng-click="toggle()"`.

exercise.task:
Complete the list in `index.html`.

- Repeat the `<li>` once for every `item` in `items` with `ng-repeat`.
- Show `{{ item.name }}` inside the `li`.
- Add `ng-class` to the `li` that is based on `item.inStock`.
- Show the "No items" paragraph only when the list is empty: use `ng-if` with a condition on `items.length`.
- Make the button call `toggle()` with `ng-click`.
hints: Each directive is an attribute. ng-repeat, ng-class and ng-click each go on the tag they should affect.
ng-repeat="item in items" on the li. ng-class takes an object such as { out: !item.inStock }. ng-if takes a condition using items.length.

• {{ item.name }}

    • No items

checks.name: The li uses ng-repeat over items
checks.hint: Add ng-repeat="item in items" to the <li>.

checks.name: ng-class depends on item.inStock
checks.hint: Add ng-class="{ out: !item.inStock }" to the li.

checks.name: The button calls toggle() with ng-click
